ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Now connect the battery pack, sliding rheostat, coil A with an iron core, coil B, galvanometer, and switch as shown in Figure 5. After the switch is closed, if coil A is inserted into coil B, what phenomenon will appear in the galvanometer pointer?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a galvanometer. The two terminals of the galvanometer are connected by wires to the two ends of coil B, so coil B and the galvanometer form a closed circuit. At the top of the figure there is a battery pack and a switch, and at the lower right there is a sliding rheostat P; they are connected to the small coil A with an iron core, so coil A is an energized coil connected in the circuit where the power supply, switch, and sliding rheostat are located. Reasoning: The question stem says that after the switch is closed, coil A is inserted into coil B. When the switch is closed, there is current in coil A, and therefore coil A produces a magnetic field. During the process of inserting A into B, the magnetic flux passing through coil B changes. According to the law of electromagnetic induction, an induced current will be produced in the closed circuit where coil B is located, so the galvanometer connected to B will have a change in reading, and the pointer will deflect.
